audience_note: Describes massacres of civilians by both sides and mass executions, including prisoners blown from cannon, and contested death tolls.

title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
summary: In May 1857 Bengal army sepoys at Meerut killed their British officers and marched on Delhi, starting a widespread revolt against East India Company rule in northern India. Fighting and British reprisals, including on civilians, continued until a peace treaty of 8 July 1858. The Company was then dissolved and the Crown assumed rule. Sources attribute more than 100,000 Indian deaths.

uncertainty.note: Royal Hampshire Regiment Museum dates the revolt May 1857 to July 1859 in one sentence but states a peace treaty on 8 July 1858 ended the rebellion; end set to 8 July 1858 and the 1859 figure noted here.

as_recorded.value: In May 1857 sepoys of the Bengal army stationed at Meerut shot their British officers
On July 8 1858, a peace treaty was signed and the rebellion ended
The first of these uprisings was in May 1857

where.modern_name: Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, India (where the revolt began)
where.historical_name: Meerut, a military station about 40 miles from Delhi under East India Company rule

importance.justification: Largest challenge to East India Company rule; led to the Company's dissolution and direct Crown rule.

reviewer_note: Death tolls are attributed and unreconciled: the museum says more than 100,000 Indians were killed; OER Project says over 50,000 sepoys and about 100,000 civilians died in suppression and revenge, plus a famine with no figure. The museum page gives both 1859 and 8 July 1858 as endpoints. Pin is Meerut but the rebellion spread across northern India; the day of the outbreak was not stated on an opened page.

beats.caption: In May 1857 sepoys at Meerut shoot their British officers and march on Delhi.
Revolt spreads across the north; on 14 September British forces storm Delhi, and civilians are killed in revenge.
A peace treaty ends the rebellion; the Company is dissolved and the Crown rules. One museum puts Indian deaths above 100,000.
